cases.title: TODEV-1885 - OW - Add Expiry Date column to Accounts History page
cases.custom_steps:
As an operator I want to see the the expiry date for each card displayed on the accounts history screen (for the cards that have it stored) and be able to filter based on this column.

 

Acceptance Criteria
Given I am viewing the Accounts History page(Customer Page) 

Then there will be a column containing the card expiry dates

And I will be able to filter the table data based on it

 

Technical Notes
We need to add the Expiry Date column into Account Summary Media Map (media details). In order to do that we must take a set of actions:

adding the new column (DB, ORM, models - DAS(which stands for “Data Aggregation Service”) & Reporting)

when saving media details here, make sure we save the expiry date as well if available (this means that we must send the information in the queue to DAS from all the writers)

Add a migration to populate the date for existing cards. This should be external, but automated from IaC - therefore ideally an endpoint or a python script - similar to other maintenance controllers - that issues media updates in DAS for all the existing medias. It should be tested for performance and documented in https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1JXHMdW2pLL8N5XMnIvuHq9sXcFMo75o9/edit#gid=987320193

Expose then the expiry date in the Reporting / OWG API that loads the users information. 

Add the column in the UI, and add it as filter in the back-end as well. 

Note that since this is going to be part of the filter, we should check if indexes need to be updated (note that it will always be used together with the PAN filter, so most likely it won’t need any updates, but it should be checked against the data used for the other stories in this epic).

cases.title: TODEV-1886 - OW - Search customer accounts by journey or payment dates
cases.custom_steps:
As an operator I want to be able to search by either journey or payment dates on the customer account screen so that I can find the customer’s account(s) more efficiently.  

 

Acceptance Criteria
Given I am viewing the Customer Account History page 

When I enter a value in the Journey Date field 

Then it will search the ‘from’ and ‘to’ fields from the Journey History page for all journeys 

And return the relevant customer account(s)



Given I am viewing the Customer Account History page 

When I enter a value in the Payment Date field 

Then it will search the ‘from’ and ‘to’ fields from the Transaction History page for all journeys 

And return the relevant customer account(s)

 




Technical Notes
These 2 filters will need to be added to the UI as inputs external to the table, similar to how the date filters exist on Reporting. They are date pickers and they can allow selecting 1 date or an interval (should be irrelevant). If one day is selected, then it represents the full day.

The filters will be implemented on the back-end as Start & End (e.g. JourneyStartDate, JourneyEndDate, TransactionStartDate, TransactionEndDate). They will represent the intervals [00:00, 00:00 next day of selected end date), e.g.

single day selected - 12/03/2024 : [12/03/2024 00:00, 13/03/2024 00:00)

multiple days selected - 12/03/2024 - 14/03/2024: [12/03/2024 00:00, 15/03/2024 00:00)

Note that, as with all the other date selectors from the UI, the dates shown are in local, but in the back-end everything is UTC, so they need to be converted.

The API from OWG and Reporting needs to be updated to accept the new properties.

The Journey Filter can be implemented by Joining the data with the JourneyHistory table (by OperatorID & MediaID). We must ensure that there’s an index for MediaID  / Operator + MediaId (to be tested with same amounts of data as other stories).

The Transaction Filter can be implemented by joining the data with the Transactions table (by OperatorId & MediaId). We must ensure that there’s an index for MediaID  / Operator + MediaId (to be tested with same amounts of data as other stories).

cases.title: TODEV-11768 - Master Card Re-Auth Process Improvement
cases.custom_steps:
Comment from SJ:
I'm not really sure if you can prove it directly - I think in live we are expecting Elavon to analyse the data we are sending to make sure they are happy with the content
You can try the steps you've suggested with the mock and Murari might be able to see if it's looking okay in the mock

Problem Statement : Retail system debt recovery(Reauthorization) having high decline rate (nearly 98% declines for Master Card).

Background: 

ABT Reprocess the retail declined transactions and sends a Deferred Auth request to NMI with card hash and card reference fields which ABT received from NMI during the first authorization. But NMI/Elavon identified that retail debt recovery might be failing because they are expecting full card information (EMV data - ICC tags) during the reauthorization as well. 

NMI/Elavon Proposed solution: 

Currently, Flowbird retrieves NMI card tokens from the initial authorization request and then resubmits them. NMI replace these tokens with PAN & Expiry data, which triggers Elavon's alert system because NMI  sending it through a card-present MID. The plan is to discontinue sending the card tokens and instead send the complete original authorization message (including EMV data) without making any other alterations to the process. This adjustment will prevent Elavon from detecting CNP data over a CP account. While we cannot guarantee that this will reduce the decline rate, providing more data in the request may help the issuer assess the transaction more effectively.

Current Approach:

Initially, transactions include EMV data but are declined.

Flowbird saves the card tokens from each attempt.

In the request for debt recovery (a Deferred Auth), we replace the token with the PAN and Expiry data, leading Elavon to classify the information as CNP over a CP MID.

This may cause issuers to struggle in recognizing these as re-attempts of a previous transaction.

 
Proposed Improvement:

We maintain the original EMV data from the initial transaction.

All re-attempts for debt recovery mirror this initial data submission.

Consequently, Elavon will process these as CP data, directly addressing your concerns about data flagging.

This modification should allow issuers to more easily identify these actions as re-attempts of the same transaction.

Technical Notes:

As per the proposed solutions , below are the changes required in ABT end ,

ABT open payment service(OPS) having an existing logic to populate the authorization request model to NMI. In that process include an extra check to add ICC tag values which already getting it from the last tap details. (OPS solution - AuthorisationRetailDebtState.cs File - GetAuthorisationRequest Method)

check is to validate whether the card brand is Master Card and type of the debt recovery is system initiated .

cases.title: TODEV-10777 - Expired Taps Report not displaying data correctly
cases.custom_steps:
The Expired Taps report is not displaying data correctly. 

There is no explanation for ETM or TID fields ? Should this dropdown be removed?

ETM and TID are not populated in the UI but contain data when exported into PDF, CSV or XLSX formats. 

Also it appears that the ETM column containts the ArchiPEL device ID of the device that sent the expired tap, should this instead be the CloudFare Device ID ?

 

Notes on fix
For rows that have count zero (0), do not show the dropdown with device data, as it will just display the headers and be confusing

Add a new field on the tap sent to TAS → FLS → JCS, in CustomData → CloudfareDeviceID and map it from transactionIdentifier.DeviceIdentifier. Then when sending over from JCS the expired tap, send this field instead of the current Device ID (which is mapped from operatingDevice.deviceIdentifier and represents the internal device id

Note: the last point is also included in the linked TODEV-11090: CLONE - MQ Tap Analysis Inconsistencies - SRUPI-996
Done
, so whichever is done first will make the field available in JCS.

cases.title: TODEV-10341: New aftercare screens
cases.custom_steps:
To Verify that New Aftercare Screen work

As an operator I want to be able to view a list of all aftercare queries and filter this list by status so that I can easily see a summary of all queries on one list as well as click on any of them to be taken to their details screen. 


 

AC1: 

Given the list is visible and contains data (default filter value is All Queries)

When I change the filter value to “Open”.

And there is at least one query open with the status of “Open” or “Pending”

Then that query or queries with those statuses are displayed in the list.  


AC2:

Given the list is visible and contains data (default filter value is All Queries)

When I change the filter value to “In Progress”.

And there is at least one query open with the status of “In Progress”, “Approved” or “Rejected”. 

Then that query or queries with those statuses are displayed in the list.  

 

AC3:

Given the list is visible and contains data (default filter value is All Queries)

When I change the filter value to “Closed”

And there is at least one query open with the status of “Closed”

Then that query or queries with that status is displayed in the list.  


AC4: 
Given the list is visible, contains data and is filtered by one of “Open”, “Approved”, “In Progress”, “Pending”, “Rejected” or “Closed”. 

When I change the filter value to ‘All Queries’.  

Then all queries are displayed in the list. 



AC5:
Given a query on the list is in ‘Open’ status

When I view the ‘Date & Time’ column for that query

Then that value is the date/time that the query was raised

 

AC6: 

Given a query on the list is in ‘In Progress’ status

When I view the ‘Date & Time’ column for that query

Then that value is the date/time of the last action on that query

 

AC7:

Given a query on the list is in ‘Closed’ status

When I view the ‘Date & Time’ column for that query

Then that value is the date/time of closure of that query

 

AC8:

Given there is a query on the list

When I left-click on the hyperlink ‘Case ID’ value 
OR I right-click and select ‘open in new window’ or ‘open in new tab’ from the right-click menu. 

Then that will take me to the aftercare details screen (in a new window or tab) for that case (query). query details within the aftercare section of the associated account 

 

AC9:
Given I have selected a case by clicking on the Case ID hyperlink and am viewing the aftercare details screen for the selected case

When I click on the back button

Then it will behave as before and not take the operator back to the aftercare dashboard




Notes: 

Point 9 step a: New Aftercare screens - “Aftercare” - new option in the left blue menu of the ABT Operator Portal under the Customers section (see screenshot Aftercare Menu Option)

On this screen (see example screenshot Aftercare Queries Screen) it should be possible using the blue horizontal arrows to filter the data between “All Queries”, “Open”, “Approved”, “In Progress”, “Pending”, “Rejected” or “Closed” (in that order) with the default being “All Queries”

Point 9 step b: The screen should consist of a table with the following columns:

Account ID

Date & Time - "Open" would be the date and time that the query was raised, "In Progress" would be the date and time of the last action, "Closed" would be the date and time of closure.

Status: Open, Approved, In Progress, Pending, Rejected or Closed. 

Operator Name: Either the Operator’s First and Surname if they raised it on behalf of a customer or ‘Customer’.if it was raised by the customer themselves. 

Case ID - This would be a hyperlink to take you to the specific case details within the Aftercare section of the associated account Correct as per point above.

Query - The most recent comment on the query or in the case of "open" queries the original query text.

Estimate: 8md


Technical notes:

New Aftercare page must be implemented and be accessible from inside Customers group menu, as shown in the second screenshot. The new Aftercare page should be displayed based on a role.

The page will have a horizontal filter and content table. The filter must be implement to look like the Users filter from Customers page, as shown in the first screenshot. To filter the data in content table, the user must be able to select from between “All Queries”, “Open”, “Approved”, “In Progress”, “Pending”, “Rejected” or “Closed” (in that order) with the default being “All Queries”.

The information displayed based on the selection in the filter must respect the AC 1 to 4. 

The content table must display the following columns: Account ID (with hyper link to Account page), Date & Time, Status, Operator Name, Case ID (means query ID), Query (query information, must be truncated if doesn't fit). 

The details of the operator which raised the query will be taken from the last comment of the query - Comment.UserID (the comment which reflects the last action on that query). If the query is raised by a passenger then the Operator Name will be empty.

Implement new aftercare endpoint to retrieve and filter Aftercare page data. Aftercare report logic can be reused for this endpoint.

Implement Date & Time logic specified in AC 5 to 7 by adding new column to Account -> Query table: the current Date column will remain as the date of the query creation, and add a new LastUpdatedTimestamp column which will be used as ‘Date & Time’ when the statuses are ‘In Progress’ or ‘Closed’. 

The ‘Case ID’ column should display the query ID as a hyper link that when clicked will take the user to the already implemented Aftercare query details screen (.../customers/customer/1/queries/1?activeTab=aftercare&activePage=1). The back button logic will behave as before and not take the operator back to the Aftercare page. (AC 8 To 9)

Note: The Status logic, meaning going from  “Open”, “Approved”, “In Progress”, “Pending”, “Rejected” to “Closed” is not part of this story.

cases.title: TODEV-10345: New aftercare screens 2: Update query status
cases.custom_steps:
Description

As an operator I want to be able to update query’s status from the list of all queries so that it is more efficient than accessing each query individually. 



AC1: 

Given the list is visible and contains data

When the status of the query on a row is “Open” or “Pending”

Then no ellipsis icon is displayed

 

 

AC2 

Given the list is visible and contains data

When the status of the query on a row is “In Progress”, “Approved” or “Rejected”

Then if I click on the ellipsis icon at the far right of a list entry the status can be changed to “Closed”


AC3:
Given the list is visible and contains data

When the status of the query on a row is “Closed”

And the original query was a ‘General Query’

Then if I click on the ellipsis icon at the far right of the row try the status can be changed to “In Progress”

 

AC4:
Given the list is visible and contains data

When the status of the query on a row is “Closed”

And the original query was a ‘Refund Request’

Then if I click on the ellipsis icon at the far right of the row try the status can be changed to “Pending”


AC4: 

Given a query is in ‘Open’ status

When I add a comment to that query

Then its status is changed to ‘In Progress’

 


Estimate: 8md

 

Technical notes:

Implement an ellipsis icon on the far right of the query row based on the status of that query. The ellipsis icon will not be displayed for “Open” or “Pending” statuses (AC 1). 

For the statuses: “In Progress”, “Approved” or “Rejected” the ellipsis will be displayed and be clickable. Add functionality when clicking the ellipsis button to change the status of the query to “Closed” (AC 2). For this logic, create new endpoint in OWGS to update the status value of the query in Account service (PATCH endpoint). In Account service the PATCH endpoint to update the status value of the query exists. 

When the status of the query is “Closed”, when clicking the ellipsis button to change the status, if the query type is ‘General Query’ then change the status to “In Progress”, if the query type is ‘Refund Request’ then change the status to “Pending”. (AC 3 to 4)

Create functionality to be able to add a comment when the status is 'Open'. Add a comment icon displayed only when the the status is 'Open'.
Implement a popup window similar to the Transactions - Refund which will appear when clicking the icon, containing a text area where to type a comment for that query and Cancel/Save buttons. When saving the comment set the status of the query to “In Progress”. (AC 5)

There is already the endpoint for adding a comment in OWGS. After the response for this call is successful call the newly created endpoint to update the status value of the query to “In Progress”.

The new LastUpdatedTimestamp column which will be used as ‘Date & Time’ when the statuses are ‘In Progress’ or ‘Closed’ should be updated when a query event is raised (when the statuses go to ‘In Progress’ or ‘Closed’).

3

cases.title: TODEV-13935 - Receive, process and pass on ICC Tag 84 (Dedicated File (DF) Name)
cases.custom_steps:
ICC Tag 84 - Dedicated File (DF) Name - will be passed in the tap message from devices (FEIG) and should then be persisted and passed on to NMI in the same way as we do with other ICC Tags. 

Notes: 
Adding this tag is a mandate from Visa. It originally had a date of 13th April 2024 but we have been granted a waiver by Visa so the date is now 15th April 2025. 

Technical Notes
Card information from devices(FEIG) reaches ABT in tap payload under the card data field and card data parses into ICC tags by using the ABTutil (TLV parser) . As per the above changes in devices(FEIG), there will be a new ICC tag information -  84 - Dedicated File (DF) Name will be added in card data and same needs to be sent to NMI while ABT invoking the NMI services. This requires below changes in  ABT.

ABT Utilis- Update ABT utils to extract the ICC tag(84 - Dedicated File (DF) Name) information from the card data , follow the same approach how its been done for other EMVtags.

Once the data populated under the ICC tag section in JTS service using the abt utils  it will be saved in JTS and same will be passed to account services and then to Open payment service to do the pre authorization with NMI through payment gateway service. But make sure the ICC tag reached until the Open payment service and during preceding taps make sure the ICC tags saved fine in LastTapData table as well in Open payment service .

During the settlement process ABT uses the Lasttapdata to send the request to NMI through payment gateway. 

Changes might require in payment gateway to populate this new flag but as per the high-level analysis this will be automatically populated if open payment sends the tag in ICC tags section of the payment request. 

Testing : TLV data can be updated to add this new flag to the existing TLV data and test this in Dev and QA regions. End to end testing will be from the System test team with the upgraded devices (FEIG)  - The details on how to update the existing TLV data is available here

Note: A1000 has confirmed that this information for the ICC tag 84 already been sent to the payment processer( Archiple) So, this change is required only for the FEIG device taps to ABT.

cases.title: TODEV-15207: CLONE - [Lothian Bus] ABT Journey Summary report having incorrect values of tram taps
cases.custom_steps:
Priority


High
Components

ABT - Transversal
Affects versions

ABT 1.2.194.3
Fix versions

ABT 1.2.200.1
Description

ABT journey summary report having incorrect values of tram taps. 

We are failing SAT tests today due to this issue. So could this be urgently investigated please. 

Technical Analysis:

Problem Summary
The current implementation of the Journey Summary Report has two critical issues causing incorrect numbers of tram taps (TOTO taps) and corresponding amounts: Production analysis here

Max Fare Journeys Not Posting to Data Aggregation:

Journeys that are charged the maximum fare are not being included in the data aggregation process, leading to missing journeys and fare amounts in the report.

Incorrect Reprocessing of Late Taps:

When a late tap occurs:

The previous journey is being reprocessed and its updated amounts are posted to data aggregation.

Both the current and previous journeys' data are incrementing journey counts and amounts incorrectly.

Expected behavior:

The previous journey data should only be updated without incrementing the amount or journey count.

The current journey should be published with the correct updated amounts.

Proposed Solution
1. Addressing Max Fare Journeys
Ensure that max fare journeys are included in the data aggregation pipeline for the Journey Summary Report.

Implementation Steps:

Identify where max fare journeys are excluded in the data aggregation logic.

Update the logic to:

Detect journeys marked as "max fare" (likely identified by a specific flag or condition).

Include them in the data aggregation pipeline.

Verify that max fare journeys are processed correctly, with their amounts and counts included in the report.

2. Correct Handling of Late Taps
Implement a robust mechanism to handle late taps that:

Updates the previous journey data without incrementing its count or amount in the report.

Publishes the current journey data with the correct values.

Implementation Steps:

   When a late tap triggers reprocessing:

Identify the Previous Journey:
Use the journey datetime as the unique identifier which is currently been used to locate the specific journey that needs to be updated in the journey summary table.

Update the Journey Summary Table:

Modify the total number of journeys and total payment amount in the journey summary table.

Instead of incrementing the counts or amounts in the aggregation pipeline, perform the following steps:

Subtract the old payment amount associated with the identified journey.

Add the new updated payment amount for the same journey.

3. Extending Functionality for All Scenarios
To ensure the solution covers all relevant scenarios, perform a comprehensive analysis of possible late tap cases:

Normal Tap: When the journey completes within the expected time.

Late Tap: When the journey crosses an operational day boundary or occurs after the expected timeframe.

Max Fare Adjustment: When a journey initially charges the max fare but later adjusts due to a late tap.

Journey Correction: When other corrections (e.g., operator-triggered adjustments) impact the journey's aggregation data.

Adjust the logic to:

Handle edge cases robustly.

Prevent duplicate or inconsistent data in the report.

Environment


None
Steps to Reproduce

None
Actual Behavior

None
Expected Behavior

cases.title: TODEV-12416: File settlement retry if an NMI pre-auth request times-out or any technical error(ex: IIN unknown)
cases.section_path: ABT / Fixes/New Features / 1.2.200 / 1.2.200 Service Now Incident Cases
cases.custom_steps:
Link to TODEV-12416: https://flowbird.atlassian.net/browse/TODEV-12416

Description

As a user I want to ensure that in the event of a pre-auth request sent to NMI (our PSP) timing out or any technical error then that it retries so that I am still charged correctly. 
Problem Statement : 

Settlements are not occurring for the open files if files stuck up on open status due to the technical errors(ex: operation time outs , IIN unknow) from NMI

Background(From the production incident analysis) : - TODEV-9860: CLONE - Translink TFTS - Disaggregated Payments On A Single Day For A User - Follow Up To INC0275050 -  [INC0285864]
Done
 

Tap received and authorization has failed with (IIN unknown or a time out from NMI). so keeping transactions in an open state.

Until this BIN updated in Elvon/NMI all the preceding transactions/taps failed with the same error. and keeping all those in an open state.

New tap received after few days , this instance Elvon/NMI corrected the issue(time out or technical error for this card) and reauthorization happened , ABT received a successful response from NMI . During the settlement process for that media. 

Solution (Which needs confirmation from NMI schema rules) : 

Retry the open files on daily basis.



AC
Given a pre-auth request has been sent to NMI 

When it times-out/ technical error from NMI

And there have been X or less previous re-try attempts for this transaction

Then send another pre-auth request

 

Technical Design Notes

The settlement process uses the GetFirstOpenFiles method from the File Manager, which uses an SQL query that specifically filters out files with errors (WHERE ERRORS is NULL or ERRORS == ‘'). What we need to do is simply remove that check from there. This will make each settlement process retry all the files that are currently open, with or without errors.

And since we are in the area, we should update the EMVAuthorisationResponse table to make the errors field actually into a JSON field (it’s text at the moment). This way we will be able to serialize directly to the error object (which is used in the AuthResponseModel but not in the entity, we need to move it to have it in both).

And we need to create an optional env var - NoRetryPspErrorCodes - which will be an array, by default empty. If provided with list of codes on this array, the settlement process will process only files with error codes that are not in the array (e.g. the join condition gets updated). Need to be careful to only include the condition when the array is provided. This will help solve eventual future production overloads in case we want to stop the retries for verious periods (e.g. we know NMI will always return this error for a month, no point in retrying).

cases.title: TODEV-15098 - Revenue Apportionment Report Amounts and %Tap Incorrect
cases.custom_steps:
High-Level Scenarios for Testing This Report
Normal Journey

A journey is created today and settled on the next operational day (after 4 AM).

Revenue apportionment should display this record only on the next operational day, not today.

Journey Correction

A journey is created and updated on the same operational day due to a late tap correction.

In this case, the journey fare amounts (latest values) and settlement amount should be displayed on the next operational day.

Re-Settlement

A journey is created today, settled the next operational day, and displayed in the revenue source for that operational day.

Due to a late tap and subsequent journey correction a few days later, there will be an update to the new charge amount.

The delta (difference) of the new charge amount should be updated at the time when the new settlement occurs for that route group.

Key Considerations:

During QA testing, negative values might appear due to fewer records in the testing environment.

In a live scenario, negative values will be very rare.

Ensure that adjustments result in positive values wherever applicable, even after corrections and settlements.

Notes for the Above Scenarios:
Revenue should align with the Revenue by MID Report.

Consider the following:

OP Journeys will only display revenue on the next operational day.

Retail Journeys will display both fare amount and settlement on the same day.

Declined transactions will not appear in the revenue source until they are settled.

For such cases, journey fare amounts update on one day, and the settlement amount updates on another day.

This behavior has been agreed upon with the project team.

cases.title: TODEV-16052 - Card Brand column is blank for some transactions
cases.custom_steps:
Technical Analysis:

This issue appears to occur with older cards that do not have an AID (Application Identifier) in the Media Manager's media data. The same applies to Lothian and Translink customers.

The story that introduced the card brand in the transaction report may also require a migration activity. This is because the AID value is not being updated when the media is updated after each authorization.

This behavior is specific to the OpenPayment (OP) flow. In contrast, the Retail flow has a different file creation mechanism, which updates the media and transaction tables differently. As a result, this issue will only affect older cards in the system that do not already have an AID populated. It is expected to be more prevalent in production, where there is a larger volume of legacy cards with empty AID values.

Solution:

Introduce update logic in both the OpenPayment Service and the Billing Service to:

Populate the AID in the Media Manager data and file model.

Ensure this update is propagated to the Data Aggregation transaction table.

This will ensure consistency in AID data and correct card brand representation in the transaction reports.

Environment


Lothian Production v201.8

Steps to Reproduce

Steps to Replicate in QA:

This issue cannot be replicated directly in the QA region, as new media or accounts are always created with a valid AID.

To simulate the issue:
Manually update the media data to have an empty AID value.
Run a few transactions.
Observe that the transaction report generates entries with an empty card brand.
Actual Behavior

The Card Brand column has numerous blank entries
Expected Behavior

The card brand column should be populated for all rows in the report

Problem Analysis and solution
Analyzed the problem in this excel - https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/13cyz-s3kTDAcxH9GpGAIRH-sTHqhGvZQrcGUaPYPDzU/edit?usp=sharingConnect your Google account .

The problem arrives when a tap that is sent for a previous day changes the aggregated & uncapped amounts of journeys without affecting their charge. Due to a system error, in this case, all the respective journeys are marked as updated and are re-sent through the file update process, rewriting their files. This results in the end of incorrect display of files and incorrect calculation of revenue sources (their charge gets double-counted). The transactions are correct.

 

How to fix
Journey Create - Update Charge Amount should post the charge update to billing only if the charge amount changed. If any other flag changed, the billing process must not be triggered, as it is just a journey update, not an actual charge update.

Data Aggregation - Revenue Sources - handles the case of payment updates wrong (Process Settlement). If the payment timestamp changed, but there are no journey corrections, then the revenue update must not be saved, because it is an incorrect state. It needs to be updated only if (1) this is the first payment OR (2) this is a different payment and there is a journey correction. Any other cases are incorrect. Anyway, with the fix from (1), this case should never be reached, but it needs to be fixed nevertheless

Note: fixing this also fixes the linked revenue sources caused by this.

Note 2: Postman collection referenced in Steps to reproduce: Postman Collections - Cloudfare ABT - Confluence

Environment


uktest-et-env2

Steps to Reproduce

1. Make sure the system runs with Reprocessing (TL/ET config)
2. Send the taps from the Postman Collection linked in the description (Taps - TOO (queue) -> TODEV-16415) in the order from the collection. The main points that reproduce the issue are:
- Send a few normal taps for yesterday
- Settle yesterday
- Send some taps for today
- Send a tap for yesterday at the beginning of the day which triggers re-processing of all taps from yesterday, but without affecting their charge (but always changing either aggregated amounts or uncapped amounts)
- Settle today
Actual Behavior

- The taps from yesterday are all added to today's file
- Revenue sources double counts the amounts already settled for yesterday, because the file is settled today and all the journeys receive updates
Expected Behavior

- The taps from yesterday which have their change unchanged remain on yesterday's file
- The taps from today & the taps that have their charge changed from yesterday (the late tap + eventual taps with charge changed) are added to today's file
- Revenue Sources shows the exact settled amount (sum of transactions)

if one journey is on 29/03 and one journey is on 31/03 → Fare band report is as expected

cases.title: TODEV-14953 - Services to subscribe to exchange from where Toplogy is published
cases.custom_steps:
Adjust logic in ABT for getting services to subscribe to the exchange in which topology is published from CloudFare. Once ABT gets new topology via this mechanism it will need to store all of the “ServiceName” results to be used in the population of services in the capping rule creation/modification screens as well as populating route group services.


Ref: Point C - ABT 8d. 
Dep: 14943

Technical Notes: 

Charge Limit

Create a consumer in the Charge Limit service that:

Reads data from the exchange:

Exchange: "topology-publish"

Routing Key: "topology-publish.config"

The services received from this exchange are cloudfare services so update the services table by setting the isCloudfare column to true.

Extract the service name from the exchange message and map it to the service code in the services table. Service ID is internal to table sequence number.

Adding New Records:

If a service is found in the exchange data but does not exist in the services table, add it as a new row.

Handling Removed Records:

If a service code exists in the services table but is no longer present in the exchange data, remove it from the AssignedService table.

Route group mapping will be automatically removed.

Removing Unnecessary Logic:

Eliminate logic that previously added new services when a new service was added to the Capping Rule or Route Group.

This is now redundant since all services are already available in the services table from the steps above.

OWG Gateway 

The OWG Gateway will directly call Charge Limit Services(/Service/{operatorId}) and display all available services from the services table.

Remove the existing validation logic for the settings 

useCloudfareServices

useChargeLimitServices

Corresponding logic across all functionalities, including:

Get Services

CappingRule AssignServices

RouteGroup AssignServices


Testing Scope: 
Post the services message in the exchange or the queue bound to the Charge Limit Service.

Validate the updates across the following screens:

Capping Rule(Add/Modify)

Route Group(Add/Remove service to route group)

Refer to the sample message body attached to the story for the correct payload structure.

cases.title: TODEV-18116: Update Operator Gateway to Invoke Fare engine with out UTF8 encoding.

Priority


Medium
Components

ABT - Operator Web - GS
Affects versions

None

25.05
ABT 1.2.209.1
Description

When ABT invokes the Fare Engine endpoint in OWG using the service redirection common functionality, it consistently encounters the following error:

ERROR FareProducts - Exception: System.FormatException: Input string was not in a correct format 

This error is being logged in the Fare Engine service.

Analysis:

The error does not occur when the same request is sent via Postman.

We removed the redirection common functionality and invoked the Fare Engine directly using BosRestClient (which does not use UTF8 encoding) — this worked correctly.

This indicates that the issue is likely due to missing or incorrect UTF8 encoding in the current redirection implementation.

Create a new redirection utility method in the utilities module that explicitly uses UTF8 encoding.

Update OWG to use this new method for Fare Engine redirection. 

Create a new repository class in OWG as similar as fare look up service call to fare engine.

Note: This issue can only be replicated in the UKTest environment, as the actual Fare Engine service is used in the UKTest region. In QA region, ABT using a general mock endpoint, and it's working as expected there.

cases.title: TODEV-16629 - Data from OP / Billing related to payment requests is not cleared down and causing slow-down
cases.custom_steps:
Steps to Reproduce

1. Have millions of journeys and settlements (production like), which generate payment requests
2. Run the daily settlement

Actual Behavior

Payment Requests are not cleared out after the normal authorization data clear-down (30d default)

Expected Behavior

Payment Requests are cleared out after the normal authorization data clear-down (30d default)

Environment


any

Description

There is a scheduled job which clears temporary data (usually related to authorizations) from the open payment table, in order to keep the system performant and to clear out data that is unusable after a (configurable) period of time.

During the development of features from 
Late Tap Reprocessingsome new tables were introduced in the two mentioned services (OPS, Billing) - mainly PaymentRequest, but the data from these is not cleared down. In Production systems the numbers have already raised quite high - for example Lothian had at the beginning of the year around 5m.

The storage of these payment requests is also causing query timeouts, especially during settlement periods, as it can be seen it’s the highest used query in Translink production environment:

Solution
Use the existing jobs to cleanup data from these tables as well.

There are a set of existing settings correlating to scheduled jobs, which do cleanup in the Billing & OP Databases:

BillingInvoicesCleanupJobAtTime

Cleans up old invoices (paid!) from Billing; this type of data needs to be stored more time. 

The setting that decides the number of days to store them is InvoicesKeepLimitDays (default 365 days)

Tables: Billing -> File, Payment, PaymentHistory 

OpenPaymentCleanupJobAtTime

Cleans up old authorization data from OPS, this data doesn’t need to be stored that long 

The setting that decides the number of days to store them is AuthorisationsTableKeepLimitDays (default is 30 days)

Tables: OP → EMVCardAuthorisationRequest, EMVCardAuthorisationResponse

PaymentInvoicesCleanupJobAtTime

Cleans up old invoices (paid!) from OPS; this type of data needs to be stored more time. 

The setting that decides the number of days to store them is InvoicesKeepLimitDays (default 365 days)

Tables: OPS → File, EMVSettlementAttempt, EMVDebtRecoveryCounter

What needs to be added / changed:

BillingInvoicesCleanupJobAtTime

Delete data from the following tables older than max(TapKeepLimitDays, AuthorisationsTableKeepLimitDays): PaymentRequest

OpenPaymentCleanupJobAtTime

Include tables: EMVCardRefundRequest, EMVTopUpAuthorisation, EMVTopUpSettlement

Delete data from these tables based older than max(TapKeepLimitDays, AuthorisationsTableKeepLimitDays): PaymentRequest, LastTapData (there should already be something that deletes last tap data)

PaymentInvoicesCleanupJobAtTime

Add RetailFileInfo to the table list (linked directly to File, so when deleting File)

Note!: we should also take a look at the two top queries and see if we have the right indexes on the PR  table.

cases.title: TODEV-18297 - Duplicate Taps: Add Infrastructure to store duplicates information
cases.custom_steps:
Rather than completely ignoring the duplicate taps, the logic needs to be amended (for both TOO and TOTO) to add store them in order to (in the linked work item) be able to display them in various reports.

Technical Notes
Add a new table in Data Aggregation called DuplicateTap:

JourneyID [long] - link to journey history

OperatorID [long]

TapID [string] - the id of the duplicate tap

ReferenceTapID [string] - the id of the tap that this one duplicates

Timestamp  [timestamptz] - date & time of the tap

LocationID [string] - location id of the tap

LocationName [string] - location name of the tap

TenantID [long] - calculated based on operator id, existing mechanism

PK: (OperatorID, JourneyID, TapID)

FK: JourneyHistory → (OperatorID, JourneyID) - note: better not to add now OperatorID because it will require changing PK for JourneyHistory, RefundRequest and JourneyCorrection as well

Data Aggregation - read from a new queue - queue.data-aggregation.duplicate-taps - a tap model in the format below, identify the existing journey based on ReferenceTapID and insert the data in the new table



{
  "OperatorID",
  "TapID",
  "ReferenceTapID",
  "Timestamp",
  "LocationID",
  "LocationName",
}
Journey Tap: If a duplicate is found (existing flow), publish the message to the new queue and discard the rest of the processing.

Tap Aggregation: when detecting a duplicate tap (existing flow), send the tap data to the new queue

cases.title: TODEV-18051 - Determine if a received tap is a Glider TOO Transfer
cases.custom_steps:
Tap Received

This indicates that a Tap On Only tap has been received from a device (whether Metro/Ulsterbus ETM or Glider PV).

 

“TransferRouteType” flag is not set to “None”?

There will be a new flag (called “TransferRouteType”) in the transaction data from the device that specifies some constraints around what the ABT back office will count as a transfer. This particular check looks to see if transfers are enabled for this tap at all. A “TransferRouteType” flag of “None” means transfers are not enabled on this tap and so the remaining transfer logic can be skipped.

 

Previous transfer applicable tap found?

This check looks for previous taps that have been received according to the following rules:

It was from the same media as the new travel tap.

The time difference between the two taps is less than or equal to the configured transfer time (expected to be 90 minutes).

The previous tap was charged (i.e. it wasn’t a transfer itself).

The “TransferRouteType” flag on the previous tap was not set to “None”.

Failure to match a tap according to any of these rules means that this new tap cannot be a transfer and so the remaining transfer logic is skipped.

 

One of the taps has “TransferRouteType” flag set to “Non-Directional”?

The system will look at the “TransferRouteType” flags for the two taps that have been matched together and if either one of them has the “TransferRouteType” flag set to “Non-Directional” then the new tap will be marked as a transfer.

 

Are the taps in the same direction?

The system will look at the “RouteDirection” flags for the two taps that have been matched together and if they both have the same direction (either “Inbound” or “Outbound”) then the new tap will be marked as a transfer.

 

Tap is charged as normal

In the case that the system has determined that a transfer is not applicable for the new tap, it will follow the typical business logic of determining the fare for the new tap i.e. whether or not it has hit any capping rules, etc.

 

Tap is not charged and marked as a transfer

If the system has determined that the new tap should be a transfer then no charge will be given for that tap and in the ABT portals the journey will be marked as a transfer using a specific transfer icon (like below) 




Technical Notes
Implement the flow described above inside the Static Transfer State from Charge Calculation Service, using the two flags from the Journey Metadata (available in Journey query, saved in the linked TODEV-18047: Add Route Direction and Transfer Route Type to the TOO Payload (JourneyTap)
Done
) to decide if the journey must be marked as transfer, alongside the already existing transfer time configuration check (keep). Note that None is to be interpreted in the same manner as null/missing.

Use the Business Rule Flow Diagram as general overview. Add a new diagram (and reference it in this one) for the particular static transfer calculation, as it begins to get more complicated.

cases.title: TODEV-17820 - Add Inspections to Tap-On Only (TOO)
cases.custom_steps:
The system should attempt to match FEIG Token from the inspection tap to TOO journey taps.  

If media exists then only match within MJT. 

If no match is found after enough time passed to trigger Standard Fare penalty then 

        Standard Fare penalty requested using existing card reference + card hash solution
Else 
        If no match found or no existing media before the MJT has expired and there has not been an authorisation for that media on that operational day then an authorisation attempt will occur. If this authorisation fails then the FEIG token will be added to both the deny and RID lists. 


Update the RID list so that it is configurable by either FEIG or ICC Tokens. N.B. Translink will use FEIG Tokens. 

Ensure the inspection success/failure and penalty fare icons for inspections are updated in the journey/transaction history screens within both the operator and passenger portals.

 

Ref: Points 2 & 3:
”Process Inspection matching for journey taps (TOO) - ABT to try to match inspection tap FEIG token with existing media. If existing media does exist then try to match it to a tap within MJT. If no match found (and waited long enough for late tap - standard fare delay) then request standard fare using existing solution. Ensure the inspection success/failure and penalty fare icons for inspections are updated in the journey/transaction history within the operator and passenger portals ”

“If no match found or no existing media by the time the maximum journey time has expired then an authorisation will occur if the payment media has not yet had an authorisation that day. If the authorisation fails then the FEIG token will be added to the deny list and RID list. This item includes the change to the RID list to make it configurable whether it contains FEIG Tokens or ICC Tokens. For Translink it will be FEIG Tokens”

 

Technical Notes
Use a similar 2-step implementation to the one that exists in Operator Gateway for Perth / FR Inspections (identify a journey inside MJT for the same media, see if it can be marked as inspection, which results in an inspection tap attached to it and in the correct inspection flags set, or if it needs to create a new journey), with the following mentions:

Step 1: Identify if there is a matching journey

Do this in JTS (after the media is identified and the tap saved in the database, right before trying to create a journey)

Since JTS has all the ‘journeys’ (taps), do the search of another journey inside JTS itself (journey-tap:1-1), for better performance, before doing any call to JCS

To account for late taps healing, when doing the search of another tap, do it for every tap (if the feature flag for inspections is enabled), not just the inspection ones, as follows:

if the current tap is an inspection (flag added in the linked work item), then search for a regular or inspection tap inside MJT right before the current one

if the current tap is not an inspection, then search for a potential standard-fare (inspection-only tap) inside MJT (this means the inspection was processed before the regular tap) right after the current one

Step 2.1 (alt): Mark the journey as inspected (if found)

When marking the journey for inspection (on the ‘journey found’ flow), there are again two cases:

if the current tap is inspection, then decorate the journey as inspected, using the existing PATCH /journey/inspection ;
this endpoint also does the journey search based on MJT, so ideally it should be changed to allow receiving in the request a TapId which, if present, overrides the journey search to be done by TapID (methods already available) (JTS should pass the TapID identified in previous step to this call) (alternative / cleaner to create a new endpoint which does the same thing)

if the current tap is non-inspection (healing), then JTS should just continue to the existing step of pushing the journey to the journey-create queue, but replacing the TapID with the existing TapId (to ensure this is interpreted as a journey update) and making sure to send over in the message the InspectionType (Inspector) and FareType (regular) to override the existing journey (JCS already has the update flow in place thanks to TOTO)

Step 2.2 (alt): Create a standard fare journey (if not found)

In the second phase, when no journey is found and the current tap is an inspection, then it means the system must issue a standard fare journey; to do this, simply push the journey to the journey-create queue as it is already done, but making sure to send over in the message the InspectionType (Inspector) and FareType (StandardFare)

If the current tap is not an inspection, this step does nothing

The main cases to test:

Regular only (exp. regular fare)

Inspection only (exp. standard fare - penalty)

Regular + Inspection inside MJT (arrives in the right order) (exp. regular fare) 

Regular + Inspection inside MJT (arrives in the reverse order) (exp. regular fare)

Inspection + Regular inside MJT (arrives in the right order) (exp. standard fare - penalty)

Inspection + Regular inside MJT (arrives in the reverse order) (exp. standard fare - penalty)

Regular + Inspection outside MJT (exp. regular fare + standard fare - penalty)

Regular + Regular + Inspection + Regular inside MJT + other variations of this (exp. regular fare)

Regular outside MJT + ( Regular + Inspection + Regular inside MJT)

The goal is to make Open Payment use the Card Reference and Card Hash to do authorizations (as CNP - Card Not Present) when the ICC Tokens and other fields are not available.

Open Payment has two places where it initiates authorizations (start of day auth if none has been done for that day), each for the different tap flows (Legacy, triggered by POST /transactions-amounts, and Reprocessing triggered by reading a Journey Payment Request from the queue), both in OpenPaymentTapManager -> AuthoriseCardAsync. The Legacy one (POST /transactions-amounts):

Update Open Payment endpoint to accept in the payload CardReference,TransactionReference and CardHash

Update Journey Create to send the CardReference, TransactionReference and CardHash (when available)

The Reprocessing (queue read for journey payment request processing):

Update the /cardinfo endpoint from Journey Query to return CardReference,TransactionReference and CardHash from OriginalTaps table (where it’s saved alongside the other fields when available, as stated in previous points)

Update Open Payment to read the new values when calling this endpoint

Handling LastTapData
Then both of their functionality unify into saving the tap data and doing the start of day authorizations. Updates:

Handling Start-of-Day Authorizations

When preparing the authorization request for Payment Gateway, attach CardReference and CardHash 

PaymentGatewayManager -> AuthoriseCard already sets the IsManualAuth flag when these fields are specified, and Payment Gateway already handles them (See Authorization flow -> Point 6 above)

Handling End of Day Authorizations

The only extra thing to do is to specify, inside PaymentGatewayManager -> SettlementAuthorize the same flag IsManualAuth to payment gateway in case only cardref + cardhash exists in tap data (to make it a cnp request).

cases.title: TODEV-17820 - Add Inspections to Tap-On Only (TOO)
cases.custom_steps:
The system should attempt to match FEIG Token from the inspection tap to TOO journey taps.  

If media exists then only match within MJT. 

If no match is found after enough time passed to trigger Standard Fare penalty then 

        Standard Fare penalty requested using existing card reference + card hash solution
Else 
        If no match found or no existing media before the MJT has expired and there has not been an authorisation for that media on that operational day then an authorisation attempt will occur. If this authorisation fails then the FEIG token will be added to both the deny and RID lists. 


Update the RID list so that it is configurable by either FEIG or ICC Tokens. N.B. Translink will use FEIG Tokens. 

Ensure the inspection success/failure and penalty fare icons for inspections are updated in the journey/transaction history screens within both the operator and passenger portals.

 

Ref: Points 2 & 3:
”Process Inspection matching for journey taps (TOO) - ABT to try to match inspection tap FEIG token with existing media. If existing media does exist then try to match it to a tap within MJT. If no match found (and waited long enough for late tap - standard fare delay) then request standard fare using existing solution. Ensure the inspection success/failure and penalty fare icons for inspections are updated in the journey/transaction history within the operator and passenger portals ”

“If no match found or no existing media by the time the maximum journey time has expired then an authorisation will occur if the payment media has not yet had an authorisation that day. If the authorisation fails then the FEIG token will be added to the deny list and RID list. This item includes the change to the RID list to make it configurable whether it contains FEIG Tokens or ICC Tokens. For Translink it will be FEIG Tokens”

 

Technical Notes
Use a similar 2-step implementation to the one that exists in Operator Gateway for Perth / FR Inspections (identify a journey inside MJT for the same media, see if it can be marked as inspection, which results in an inspection tap attached to it and in the correct inspection flags set, or if it needs to create a new journey), with the following mentions:

Step 1: Identify if there is a matching journey

Do this in JTS (after the media is identified and the tap saved in the database, right before trying to create a journey)

Since JTS has all the ‘journeys’ (taps), do the search of another journey inside JTS itself (journey-tap:1-1), for better performance, before doing any call to JCS

To account for late taps healing, when doing the search of another tap, do it for every tap (if the feature flag for inspections is enabled), not just the inspection ones, as follows:

if the current tap is an inspection (flag added in the linked work item), then search for a regular or inspection tap inside MJT right before the current one

if the current tap is not an inspection, then search for a potential standard-fare (inspection-only tap) inside MJT (this means the inspection was processed before the regular tap) right after the current one

Step 2.1 (alt): Mark the journey as inspected (if found)

When marking the journey for inspection (on the ‘journey found’ flow), there are again two cases:

if the current tap is inspection, then decorate the journey as inspected, using the existing PATCH /journey/inspection ;
this endpoint also does the journey search based on MJT, so ideally it should be changed to allow receiving in the request a TapId which, if present, overrides the journey search to be done by TapID (methods already available) (JTS should pass the TapID identified in previous step to this call) (alternative / cleaner to create a new endpoint which does the same thing)

if the current tap is non-inspection (healing), then JTS should just continue to the existing step of pushing the journey to the journey-create queue, but replacing the TapID with the existing TapId (to ensure this is interpreted as a journey update) and making sure to send over in the message the InspectionType (Inspector) and FareType (regular) to override the existing journey (JCS already has the update flow in place thanks to TOTO)

Step 2.2 (alt): Create a standard fare journey (if not found)

In the second phase, when no journey is found and the current tap is an inspection, then it means the system must issue a standard fare journey; to do this, simply push the journey to the journey-create queue as it is already done, but making sure to send over in the message the InspectionType (Inspector) and FareType (StandardFare)

If the current tap is not an inspection, this step does nothing

The main cases to test:

Regular only (exp. regular fare)

Inspection only (exp. standard fare - penalty)

Regular + Inspection inside MJT (arrives in the right order) (exp. regular fare) 

Regular + Inspection inside MJT (arrives in the reverse order) (exp. regular fare)

Inspection + Regular inside MJT (arrives in the right order) (exp. standard fare - penalty)

Inspection + Regular inside MJT (arrives in the reverse order) (exp. standard fare - penalty)

Regular + Inspection outside MJT (exp. regular fare + standard fare - penalty)

Regular + Regular + Inspection + Regular inside MJT + other variations of this (exp. regular fare)

Regular outside MJT + ( Regular + Inspection + Regular inside MJT)

All the authorizations part described in this story are handled inside the linked TODEV-17645: Accept decoded card details (Token, CardRef, CardHash, PAR) and Inspection flag in (inspection) tap payload
Done
. This can be the place to (re) test them with proper inspection handling in UI as well (as the linked item treats auths only). First Tap Flow, Standard Fare delayed payment handling and the rest are already part of the system.

Handling the right tokens on the RID List is handled by the linked TODEV-18129: Allow RID List to use different types of tokens (EMV2 instead of ICCToken, but generalize)
Done

cases.title: TODEV-17822 - Configure default boarding/alighting stages for penalty fares for MERIT
cases.custom_steps:
Add the option to be able to configure a boarding and alighting stage for MERIT.  This additional data is required by MERIT for inspection taps*.  

With an inspection there are no boarding or alighting stages hence it is necessary to send a default stage ID for both boarding and alighting. 

These will be configured via the database. 

* Or in the future, TOTO journeys with a missing tap on.

 

AC1

Given a penalty fare has been charged

When the system sends the transaction to merit

Then it populates the missing stages as follows:

both stages as default if both are missing

alighting if one is missing and there is no known Gate Direction

boarding or alighting if one is missing and there is a known Gate Direction

 

Ref: Point 7. 

“Configure default boarding/alighting stage for MERIT - In order for inspection taps (or in the future, TOTO journeys with a missing tap on) to be sent to MERIT they require additional data. In particular, with an inspection there are no boarding or alighting stages so it is necessary to send a default stage ID for both of those values - this will need to be configured via the database”

Technical Notes
Add two new settings - DefaultBoardingStage and DefaultAlightingStage - with values as JSON objects in a similar manner to the contents of the tap location zone: 



 {
    "ID": "dummy-boarding/alighting-id",
    "Name": "Dummy Boarding / Alighting Name",
    "Zones": [
      {
        "ID": "dummy-boarding/alighting-zone-id"
      }
    ]
 }
Migrate (with data) the existing settings (and their usage) AlightingStageZoneId and BoardingStageZoneId to the new settings and discard them & their previous usage starting with the new version (impacts mostly SCS migration and JTS/JCS)

Update Data Aggregation  MERIT sender - if it detects a penalty fare to do the following thing:

if the journey is missing both tap on and tap off (e.g. it has only inspection tap) → use both default stages

if the journey is missing only one tap, but the existing tap has a known GateDirection, then use the corresponding default stage

if the journey is missing only one tap, but the existing tap does not have a known GateDirection, then use the default alighting

Update the documentation

Update IaC & Helm

For testing - test the new AC, but also test the regression in regards to the usage of the existing two settings (used in A1000/transaction taps only)

cases.title: TODEV-18051 - Determine if a received tap is a Glider TOO Transfer
cases.custom_steps:
Tap Received

This indicates that a Tap On Only tap has been received from a device (whether Metro/Ulsterbus ETM or Glider PV).

 

“TransferRouteType” flag is not set to “None”?

There will be a new flag (called “TransferRouteType”) in the transaction data from the device that specifies some constraints around what the ABT back office will count as a transfer. This particular check looks to see if transfers are enabled for this tap at all. A “TransferRouteType” flag of “None” means transfers are not enabled on this tap and so the remaining transfer logic can be skipped.

 

Previous transfer applicable tap found?

This check looks for previous taps that have been received according to the following rules:

It was from the same media as the new travel tap.

The time difference between the two taps is less than or equal to the configured transfer time (expected to be 90 minutes).

The previous tap was charged (i.e. it wasn’t a transfer itself).

The “TransferRouteType” flag on the previous tap was not set to “None”.

Failure to match a tap according to any of these rules means that this new tap cannot be a transfer and so the remaining transfer logic is skipped.

 

One of the taps has “TransferRouteType” flag set to “Non-Directional”?

The system will look at the “TransferRouteType” flags for the two taps that have been matched together and if either one of them has the “TransferRouteType” flag set to “Non-Directional” then the new tap will be marked as a transfer.

 

Are the taps in the same direction?

The system will look at the “RouteDirection” flags for the two taps that have been matched together and if they both have the same direction (either “Inbound” or “Outbound”) then the new tap will be marked as a transfer.

 

Tap is charged as normal

In the case that the system has determined that a transfer is not applicable for the new tap, it will follow the typical business logic of determining the fare for the new tap i.e. whether or not it has hit any capping rules, etc.

 

Tap is not charged and marked as a transfer

If the system has determined that the new tap should be a transfer then no charge will be given for that tap and in the ABT portals the journey will be marked as a transfer using a specific transfer icon (like below)

TODEV-16629 - Data from OP / Billing related to payment requests is not cleared down and causing slow-down
cases.custom_steps:
Solution
Use the existing jobs to cleanup data from these tables as well.

There are a set of existing settings correlating to scheduled jobs, which do cleanup in the Billing & OP Databases:

BillingInvoicesCleanupJobAtTime

Cleans up old invoices (paid!) from Billing; this type of data needs to be stored more time. 

The setting that decides the number of days to store them is InvoicesKeepLimitDays (default 365 days)

Tables: Billing -> File, Payment, PaymentHistory 

OpenPaymentCleanupJobAtTime

Cleans up old authorization data from OPS, this data doesn’t need to be stored that long 

The setting that decides the number of days to store them is AuthorisationsTableKeepLimitDays (default is 30 days)

Tables: OP → EMVCardAuthorisationRequest, EMVCardAuthorisationResponse

PaymentInvoicesCleanupJobAtTime

Cleans up old invoices (paid!) from OPS; this type of data needs to be stored more time. 

The setting that decides the number of days to store them is InvoicesKeepLimitDays (default 365 days)

Tables: OPS → File, EMVSettlementAttempt, EMVDebtRecoveryCounter

What needs to be added / changed:

BillingInvoicesCleanupJobAtTime

Delete data from the following tables older than max(TapKeepLimitDays, AuthorisationsTableKeepLimitDays): PaymentRequest

OpenPaymentCleanupJobAtTime

Include tables: EMVCardRefundRequest, EMVTopUpAuthorisation, EMVTopUpSettlement

Delete data from these tables based older than max(TapKeepLimitDays, AuthorisationsTableKeepLimitDays): PaymentRequest, LastTapData (there should already be something that deletes last tap data)

PaymentInvoicesCleanupJobAtTime

Add RetailFileInfo to the table list (linked directly to File, so when deleting File)

cases.title: TODEV-23967 - Issue when performing annulments with duplicate taps
cases.custom_steps:
Another issue has been spotted with ABT v228.3 and duplicate tap logic. I was testing a scenario for Metro and Ulsterbus annulments with duplicate taps which resulted in the ABT back office capping incorrectly.

Please see detail and steps below:

Metro Scenario:

I Tapped on Metro ETM at 11:20:56 on 9A (OUT) service (first stage Bedford St, default alighting stage Conway). I watched the tap hit the ABT back office before annulling the tap:

Tapped at 11:20:56, Metro tap hits ABT back office

image-20260415-084010.png
Annulled Metro tap. Annulment displayed in customer account:

image-20260415-084024.png
Tapped again at Bedford St at 11:22. Once tap hits ABT, it is flagged as a duplicate tap (believe this logic is correct as tap was performed at same boarding stage as annulled tap at 10:20:56). However, notice how charge amount is shown as £0.00 for annulled tap but should show £2.30 (as 11:22 tap is the first “good” tap of the day)

image-20260415-084041.png
Tapped again at 11:25:41 at a different stage to test Metro Daily Cap. This tap appears to be audited as the first tap of the day so charge amount is £2.30. This should be showing £1.70 and Metro Daily Cap applied.

image-20260415-084056.png
Tapped again at 11:32:33 and Metro Daily Cap is applied and charge amount £1.70 (this should be a £0.00 “free” tap) as third successful tap of the day

image-20260415-084117.png
Steps to replicate:

Tap on Metro ETM running v1.2.2 and ABT v228.3

Annul tap

Tap again at same boarding stage. Check ABT portal – notice how duplicate tap has been flagged and charge amount is £0.00 (should be £2.30). I suspect this is due to the first tap being annulled and showing £0.00 therefore second tap being flagged as duplicate and ABT back office is not treating it as a successful tap.

Tap again at a separate boarding stage, notice how this tap then audits at £2.30 instead of £1.70 for second “good” tap of the day.

Tap again (3rd successful tap), notice how tap is audited as £1.70 instead of £0.00

Ulsterbus Scenario:

I also checked this in Ulsterbus for Reference Fare capping and issue also occurs. Annulling the first ref fare tap then tapping again at same boarding stage causes the first good tap to basically be cleared in terms of charge amount. Please see example below from UB:

 

First tap was 61 (OUT) route at 12:20:48 from Rushemere Shopping Centre to Mullaghbane Crossroads for £4.00. Tap was annulled within 1 minute

Tapped again at 12:11 from same boarding stage but changed alighting stage and reference fare value (Rushmere Shopping Centre – Annaclare £4.50) . ABT flagged this tap as duplicate and no charge amount displayed

Changed alighting stage to Craigavon Area Hospital at 12:23:55 and issued TOO DI tap to Armagh Buscentre for £4.50. This then audited as the first tap towards the ref.60 Daily Cap (should have registered as second ref.60 tap and applied £7.20 cap)

Tapped on a different route with £4.50 ref fare value and cap applied (this was the 3rd £4.50 tap for this account but ABT is treating it as the second)

image-20260415-084145.png
The scenario above for Metro is probably unlikely to happen (customer taps at stage, driver annuls then customer taps at same stage again) but the Ulsterbus scenario could happen where a customer boards a bus, driver accidentally selects the wrong alighting stage, annuls and customer taps again from same boarding stage.

cases.title: TODEV-24096 - ABT - Metro Daily Cap Is Removed After Updating Stop Location on a Settled Tap
cases.custom_steps:
An issue has been identified where the Metro daily cap is incorrectly removed from a transaction. This occurs when the stop location of a tap is updated after the tap has already been settled and had the daily cap applied.

Steps to Reproduce:

A passenger performs a tap that results in the Metro daily cap being reached.

The tap transaction is settled by the system.

An administrator or process updates the stop location for that settled tap.

Expected Result:
The daily cap should remain applied to the transaction, and the fare should not be recalculated to exceed the cap.

Actual Result:
The daily cap is removed from the tap. This can lead to the passenger being overcharged if fares are recalculated.

cases.title: TIBU-23390: Merit Web Reporter: When 'All' is ticked for all Days of the week then all the days of the week should also be ticked
cases.section_path: Merit Web Reporter / Fixes/Changes / MERIT Web Improvements/Bug Fixing
cases.custom_steps:
Description

Merit Web Reporter: When 'All' is ticked for all Days of the week then all the days of the week should also be ticked

Merit Web  Reporter Version: 1.1.105.1

Environment: On Prem

Time Stamp 08:20

Steps to Reproduce

Load Merit Web Reporter

Select Annulled Ticket Report

Select the Start and End Date of the Report

Leave Days of the week Ticked but with all days of the week unticked as default

Select Location, Staff and Devices

Run The Report

Expected Result

Merit Web Report should run the report

Actual Result

Merit Web Report displays an 'Invalid Selections for Report: Date message at the top of the screen

If the user unticks the All box and then ticks it again, all the dates(Sunday through Saturday) are now ticked  

Environment


None
Closure Reason


None
Requirements


None

cases.title: TIBU-23391: Merit Web Reporter - Selecting Run button while a report is already displayed causes the report to crash
cases.section_path: Merit Web Reporter / Fixes/Changes / MERIT Web Improvements/Bug Fixing
cases.custom_steps:
Description

Merit Web Reporter ???

Selecting Run button while a report is already displayed causes the report to crash.

This issue occurs for every report.

Unable to get report parameters. Report '%7B%22ReportName%22%3A%22Daily%20Audit%22%2C%22OperatorName%22%3Anull%2C%22OperatorId%22%3A0%2C%22UserSelectorCacheKey%22%3A%22UserSelector_n5iueryduggssu0toy1lcvw0%22%7D' cannot be resolved.

Steps to reproduce:

Select a report on Merit Web Reporter

Fill out each criteria section for the report selected 

Select the Run button

After the report has fully loaded select the Run button again

Expected Result:

Report reloads/refreshes when selecting the Run button a second time

Actual Result:

Report crashes when selecting the Run button a second time

cases.title: AFCBOS-3713 - Adds stored procedure used  for the Synchronization of CloudFare staff details into Merit
cases.custom_steps:
Upon one of the below two actions occurring the new/modified staff data must be sent to MERIT:

- Staff data modified (and saved) in staff manager in CloudFare
- New staff member added to staff manager in CloudFare

Synchronisation mechanism:

- CloudFare must send a list of the staff that have changed to a message queue. These changes will be specifically for the staff member that was added/modified but there will be individual records per location for their home location and each working location they are assigned to.
- MERIT Integration must pick up the list of changes from the message queue, translate the CloudFare location codes into MERIT location codes and call a stored procedure in MERIT to import the records into the database.
- The stored procedure must check it the staff number and location code combination already exists. If so, it must update the staff name associated to that combination. If it doesn’t exist then it must add a new record to the database.

It has been said that all existing staff will not be updated so this is only applying to new staff added or updated in cloudfare.

cases.title: UKCSMB-1781 - Flowbird Transport Intelligence - Staff Synchronisation to CloudFare - Glider [INC0287593]
cases.custom_steps:
Can a ticket be raised for Heath Barnard to look at to implement the following:

Functionality has previously been added to CloudFare (see linked work item - https://flowbird.atlassian.net/browse/UKCAFCBOS-3713) to synchronise staff data created in CloudFare (or imported into CloudFare) to MERIT.

Having tested this functionality it has been noted that the Glider depot staff numbers are not being synchronised as they require because they have some special logic for Glider that was not captured in the original requirements for the above.

When synchronising other data to MERIT (i.e. shifts, transactions, etc.) there is a conditional check to add a prefix of "96" to all staff members if they belong to the Glider depot. We require this check to be performed for staff synchronisation to MERIT also.

------------------------------
h3. Relevant Information for this ticket:

Steps to Reproduce

Go to Staff Manager in CloudFare

Add a staff member with a 4 digit staff number that is assigned to the “Glider (Metro)” home location

Expected
Staff member gets synchronised to MERIT and the staff number in MERIT is a 6 digit number (the 4 digit staff number prefixed with “96”)

Actual
Staff member gets synchronised to MERIT and the staff number in MERIT is the 4 digit staff number

cases.title: TIBU-17536 - Implement changes to Tickets By Operator report to meet requirements for CR078 - TEST 1: Transaction data reporting
cases.custom_steps:
In the linked story CloudFare (& MERIT Integration) is going to get functionality to send diagnostic records to MERIT for a specific set of events that contain data needed to populate the Tickets By Operator report in MERIT.

MERIT needs to be updated to:

Consume these diagnostic records (if applicable - I think MERIT already supports diagnostic records as we’re using the same legacy format as legacy devices used to send)

Utilise these diagnostic records together with transactions with a payment type of “BarcodeUsage” to calculate new values for each staff member in the Tickets By Operator report (see example of current report below and further details of what the new total needs to comprise of)

Note that the format of the Tickets By Operator report will stay the same so we expect to retain the initial columns for Staff No, Location and Name and then the split of totals by week with an overall total at the end of the line.

Current Tickets By Operator report:

![](index.php?/attachments/get/223715)

New Totals by Staff Member and by Location are the sum of:

Electronic inspections of smartcards - via new diagnostic records (event codes 5000 and 5001)

Electronic validations of smartcards - should be what the report already contains (think this is counted via the PassCount variable)

Paper ticket issues - should be what the report already contains (think this is counted via the TicketCount variable)

Electronic validations of single-use barcodes - via new diagnostic records (event codes 1412 and 1416)

Electronic validations of multi-use barcodes - via transactions with a payment type of “BarcodeUsage”

Note that this will be extended for cEMV inspections to be included in the total in the future so if we can make sure it’s easy to add an extra diagnostic code into the total that would be great.

cases.title: TIBU-17983 - Merit bug in trigger trg_d_Trans on the trans table (INC0248205)
cases.custom_steps:
An error has been found in one of the triggers on the Trans table in the Merit database. Can you create an issue for this please and from that raise an SMB. Have Peter Weeks assign it to me please. Below is the text that describes the issue.

There is an issue with the trigger trg_d_Trans on the trans table. In the other triggers on the Trans table (trg_i_Trans and trg_u_Trans), the TransSummary.int4_SummaryClassCount value is calculated as TransSummary.int4_SummaryClassCount - transaction class count. For transactions that have positive values (i.e. revenue, nonrevenue, ticket count and pass count) then the transaction class count is 1. If negative transaction values (i.e. and annulment transaction) then the transaction class count value is -1.

The trigger trg_d_Trans just subtracts 1 from the TransSummary.int4_SummaryClassCount value irrespective if the transaction is an annulment or not.
As an example, if there are 4 transactions that make up a single TransSummary record and 3 have positive values and 1 has negative values then the TransSummary.int4_SummaryClassCount should be 2. If you delete only the transaction with the negative values then TransSummary.int4_SummaryClassCount should be 3. If you delete only one of the transactions with positive values then TransSummary.int4_SummaryClassCount should be 1. If you delete one transaction with positive values and the transaction with negative values then TransSummary.int4_SummaryClassCount should be 2.

The same applies to the JourneySummary table although that does not appear in the trg_u_Trans trigger for some reason.

This has been an issue for at least the last 17 years but transactions never deleted so this has not raised itself before. The TransSummary.int4_SummaryClassCount and JourneySummary.int4_SummaryClassCount columns are used in quite a few Translink specific views and stored procedures so we need to get this fixed before the transaction deletion script being written for https://flowbird.atlassian.net/browse/SMB-1153#icft=SMB-1153 can be used

We have now had feedback from Stevie Chambers following his evaluation of Smatrack CMS and he has highlighted that there are 2 show stoppers as detailed below;

Operator ID:
In the “transactions” tab against the history of a card, he can’t see a field for “Operator ID”. See below screenshot from their existing Smartrack – this field is important when reconciling sales of new passes and/or replacement passes in our retail locations, which is done via PC POS. Having an ID that they can trace back to whoever the member of staff helped resolve disputes/training issues/mistakes etc, and is pretty fundamental to providing good customer service when an issue is encountered.

image 1.png

Stevie has asked if this isn’t tracked here, is there another field that might have the same details?

Expiry Date:
This is a similar issue to the above Operator ID. The transactions tab no longer appears to have a field tracking the change in the expiry date of any active product. The front page of any card/customer record shows the expiry date of the token and this is what we use in the first instance when dealing with issues or card replacements.
